data.gender_notes: Amirahd is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A leader, a commander, one who guides and directs others. The name Amirahd carries the meaning “Leader, Commander” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Amirahd usually hope their child will grow to embody leader, commander and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who is guided by Allah
data.etymology: Amirahd belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Leader, Commander.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amirahd total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: أميرةذ
in_arabic.long_meaning: يأتي اسم أميرةذ من الجذر العربي "أَمِير"، المُشتق من كلمتين "أَمَ" و"رِياذ"، تُشير إلى الحامل للمجد والشرف، حيث كان الأمير في المجتمع الإسلامي رمزًا للسلطة والمجد. في العصر الحديث، يستخدم اسم أميرةذ في العديد من الثقافات الإسلامية كعنوان للمرأة، يرمز إلى الكرم والأمانة. يرتبط اسم أميرةذ بتقاليد العائلة والثروة والسمعة، ويصاحبها احترام وเคفاءة. يعتبر اسم أميرةذ من الأسماء الإسلامية الشائعة، ويتميز بروعه وعمق معانيه في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_hindi.name: अमीरहद
in_hindi.meaning: अमीरहद का अर्थ है शानदार और श्रेष्ठ
in_hindi.long_meaning: अमीरहद नाम का उद्गम अरबी जड़ "अमीर" से हुआ है, जिसका अर्थ है "अमीर" और "रियाज़" जो शानदार और श्रेष्ठ के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। इस्लामी संस्कृति में, अमीर एक राजा या शासक के लिए एक उपाधि के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता था जो धन और शान का प्रतीक था। अमीरहद नाम का उपयोग भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में है। यह नाम एक महिला के लिए एक शानदार और अच्छा नाम है।

in_english.name: Amirahd
in_english.meaning: Amirahd means noble and honored, a symbol of power and prestige
in_english.long_meaning: The name Amirahd is derived from the Arabic root "Amir", which means "noble" and "honored", referring to the holder of power and prestige. In Islamic tradition, the title of Amir was used to signify a ruler or leader who embodied the values of dignity and honor. The name Amirahd has been adopted in various Muslim cultures, symbolizing the qualities of nobility, dignity, and prestige. It is often associated with positive traits such as confidence, leadership, and compassion.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Amirahd" carries a strong cultural identity as it signifies a powerful and influential leader in the Islamic context. This name, derived from the Arabic word "Amir", meaning commander or prince, has historical connotations of royalty, authority, and wisdom. In many Islamic societies, the title "Amir" was given to prominent scholars, military leaders, and political figures. The name "Amirahd" may also symbolize spiritual and moral leadership, emphasizing the importance of a just and virtuous ruler in building a strong and resilient community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Amirahd" also holds significant spiritual value in Islam. In the Islamic tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is often described as the "Commander of the Faithful" or "Amir al-Mu'minin." The Quran, the sacred text of Islam, repeatedly emphasizes the importance of leadership, guidance, and unwavering obedience to God, encouraging the faithful to follow the path of the righteous leaders. By bestowing the name "Amirahd" upon a child, parents may be expressing their aspirations for their child to embody the virtues of a true leader and to lead a life that is guided by spiritual wisdom and moral values.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Leader, Commander" symbolizes A leader, a commander, one who guides and directs others.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Amirahd serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of leader, commander.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Amirahd was the daughter of the 10th Abbasid Caliph, Al-Musta'sim Billah (1242-1257). The name Amirahd carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Amirahd was a prominent figure in the Abbasid Caliphate during the Mongol invasion.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Amirahd remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
